title: Machine learning links neighborhood context to acute coronary diagnoses
summary: A random forest evaluated acute coronary syndrome in 2,400 emergency chest-pain patients using demographics, medical history and neighborhood measures. A held-out 720-patient test supported an AUC of 0.71, while regularized regression retained a neighborhood association after adjustment. Diagnoses were independently adjudicated. These single-city observational results do not establish causal neighborhood effects, individual income effects or benefit from model-guided triage.

source_review.scope: Primary relevant Methods/results/limitations and exact front/canonical identity; current primary PubMed linked correction/retraction metadata checked.

evidence.tested: Training-only tuning, a 30% patient test set and blinded physician adjudication of acute coronary syndrome.
evidence.unknown: External transportability, causal social effects and clinical triage benefit remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Random forests rank nonlinear clinical/geospatial predictors; regularized regression evaluates adjusted neighborhood associations.
